name: Lip flip (Botox)
lead: A lip flip is a cosmetic procedure in which small amounts of botulinum toxin type A are injected superficially along the upper lip border, relaxing part of the orbicularis oris muscle so the upper lip rolls slightly outward and upward. The result is a little more pink lip showing, a softer or more defined upper-lip contour and an impression of fullness, without adding volume [1][2][14].

People use it to make a thin upper lip look fuller, to rebalance upper-lip proportions, to soften vertical lip lines, and in some cases to reduce the amount of upper gum shown when smiling [2][13][6]. Because it relaxes muscle rather than adding material, it is often presented as a reversible alternative or complement to hyaluronic acid filler, with effects described as lasting a few months [4][6][10].

The technique is an off-label use of botulinum toxin and the literature is young. It consists of technique descriptions, case series, a 2025 systematic review that identified seven eligible articles, and a 2026 prospective study of 17 women that measured upper-lip height with stereophotogrammetry [1][3][4][2]. Search interest in the term grew steadily between 2014 and 2024 [10]. The words "lip flip" are also used in some papers for a different, filler-based technique [7].

paras: The orbicularis oris encircles the mouth and closes and purses the lips. It is innervated by the facial nerve and, rather than a true sphincter, is made of interlacing fibres from several directions; the philtrum sits between the two central bands of the upper lip [16]. In a lip flip, a clinician places very small superficial injections of toxin along the upper lip border near the vermilion, aiming at the marginal part of the muscle [14][1]. A 2026 short report describes an anatomical rationale of partially relaxing the pars marginalis while avoiding the mouth corners and deeper muscle layers [14].

Botulinum toxin blocks the release of acetylcholine at the nerve ending, so the muscle relaxes; the blockade wears off as the nerve terminal regenerates the proteins the toxin cleaves [15]. In the cosmetic setting, effects usually appear in days and typically last two to four months, so treatments are repeated to maintain the look [15]. A summary on Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, gives similar timing for the lip flip and notes it may also reduce the look of a gummy smile; that page is treated as unverified [6].

The phrase "lip flip" is not used consistently. Most literature uses it for the toxin technique [1][4]. A 2022 paper reports a different method with the same name, a cannula-based hyaluronic acid filler technique for perioral rejuvenation, evaluated in 70 women; the upper white lip distances shortened significantly after treatment [7]. Wikipedia describes the lip flip as toxin along the vermilion border, sometimes combined with filler for extra volume [12]. Gelada monkeys also have a facial display called a lip-flip, which is unrelated [8].

A 2026 case series of 45 patients described a variant that places toxin at lateral points of the orbicularis oris, based on a balance between the risorius and orbicularis oris muscles, to alter apparent lip width; 37 of 45 rated improvement at three or more on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale, and the author notes objective widening and functional safety were not measured [9]. A 2025 review of perioral rejuvenation lists the lip flip among neurotoxin applications alongside perioral wrinkles, oral commissure elevation, dimpled chin and gummy smile [13].

The lip flip builds on the broader history of cosmetic botulinum toxin. Plastic surgeon Richard Clark of Sacramento reported the first aesthetic use in 1989, correcting an asymmetric forehead after a facelift, and J. D. and J. A. Carruthers studied the toxin for frown lines in 1992 [15]. The FDA approved Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines in 2002, after cosmetic use was already widespread [15].

The medical literature on the lip flip appears in the early 2020s: a 2021 review and a 2021 letter on the neurotoxin lip flip, followed by a 2025 systematic review, reviews of public interest and prospective studies in 2025-2026 [1][3][4][10][2]. The authors of one 2021 article noted that little had been published on the trend and set out to check whether interest in it was truly rising [1].

Published human data are limited and mostly descriptive. A 2025 systematic review in Archives of Dermatological Research searched PubMed and Ovid, found 48 articles and included seven that reported injection sites and dosages. It found consistent upper-lip eversion and improved contour without added volume, high patient satisfaction and little downtime, and mild, temporary adverse effects such as difficulty whistling or drinking through a straw that resolved within weeks; the authors called the technique minimally invasive with a good safety profile [4].

A 2026 prospective study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery treated 17 women with standardized upper-lip neuromodulation and measured results with stereophotogrammetry. Upper-lip height increased modestly but significantly at 15 days, lip volume did not change, perioral appraisal scores improved, and satisfaction was high; adverse events were mild and transient, including temporary numbness and functional limitation, resolving within 30 days. The authors concluded that the effect comes from selective muscle neuromodulation rather than added volume [2].

A 2026 short report in JPRAS Open described three consecutive patients treated superficially along the upper-lip border with letibotulinumtoxinA; at two weeks all had a mild lip lift and fewer vertical lines, none reported speech problems or asymmetry, and the authors cautioned that the sample was very small, uncontrolled and unblinded [14]. A 2021 case series in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology and a 2021 Journal of Craniofacial Surgery review also describe the technique [3][1]. A 2025 Google Trends analysis found searches for both lip filler and lip flip rose from 2014 to 2024, with lip filler searched more but lip flip growing, which the authors suggest makes it a possible alternative for patients hesitant about filler [10]. No randomized trial comparing the lip flip with fillers has been published.

Toxin placed near the mouth can affect neighbouring muscles. The clinical literature reports temporary difficulty whistling, drinking through a straw, numbness and mild functional limitation, and discusses asymmetry and effects on speech, drinking and smiling as the kind of issue that can follow weakening of the orbicularis oris [4][2][1]. More generally, unintended spread of cosmetic botulinum toxin can cause partial facial paralysis and muscle weakness, and the FDA added boxed warnings about toxin spread in 2009 [15].

Because the lip flip is off-label, labelling does not describe it; medical sources describe it as performed by clinicians who understand perioral anatomy [1][13]. The 2026 case series on lateral injections notes that systematic safety assessment is still needed [9].

Users on looksmax.org have written guides describing the lip flip as targeting a thin upper lip, a long philtrum, a crooked lip and proportions such as facial width-to-height ratio and chin-to-philtrum ratio, and as a way to rebalance the upper lip. One guide cites a study on filler and perceived lip attractiveness to argue that fuller lips are rated as more attractive in thin-lipped patients [11]. Some threads also discuss obtaining toxin outside clinics and injecting it oneself; this wiki does not summarize those methods. Medical sources describe the procedure as one done by clinicians [1][13].

timeline.event: Richard Clark reports the first aesthetic use of botulinum toxin, correcting an asymmetric forehead after a facelift.[15]
The Carruthers study botulinum toxin for frown lines.[15]
The FDA approves Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines.[15]
The FDA adds boxed warnings about toxin spreading from the injection site.[15]
A review and a case series on the neurotoxin lip flip are published.[1][3]
A separate filler-based technique called the lip flip is reported in 70 women.[7]
A systematic review of botulinum toxin lip augmentation and a review of perioral rejuvenation are published; a Google Trends study compares lip filler and lip flip interest.[4][13][10]
A prospective study of 17 women, a three-patient report and a lateral-injection case series add data.[2][14][9]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the lip flip appears in guides as an inexpensive, reversible option for upper-lip proportions, tied to ratios such as philtrum length and chin-to-philtrum ratio [11].

claims.claim: A lip flip can make a thin upper lip look fuller and change facial proportions.
claims.believers: A forum guide says the injections roll the lip upward and outward and lists benefits such as improved lip proportions, a more compact midface, an apparently shorter philtrum and a better chin-to-philtrum ratio [11].
claims.experts: A 2026 prospective study found a modest but significant increase in upper-lip height and high satisfaction, with no change in volume [2]; the 2025 systematic review reports consistent eversion and improved contour [4].

claims.claim: The effect is temporary and reversible.
claims.believers: Forum users present it as a low-commitment trial of how a different lip shape would look [11].
claims.experts: Descriptions of cosmetic botulinum toxin report effects lasting roughly two to four months, and reported lip-flip side effects resolved within weeks [15][4][2].

claims.believers: Guides describe it as an alternative to filler for people who want subtle change [11].
claims.experts: The study using stereophotogrammetry found lip volume unchanged, with the apparent change coming from height and eversion; reviewers describe it as enhancing contour without adding volume [2][4].

claims.claim: A lip flip can fix a crooked lip.
claims.believers: A forum guide title and text say it makes the lip less crooked and more balanced [11].
claims.experts: Published studies describe eversion and contour in small groups; a case series on lateral injections for lip width says objective measurement and functional safety were not assessed [4][9].

claims.claim: The injection can be self-administered at home.
claims.believers: Forum threads discuss doing it themselves [11].
claims.experts: The published literature describes the procedure as performed by clinicians and discusses the anatomical balance of the muscles around the mouth [1][9].

claims.claim: Lip flip is becoming a mainstream rival to lip filler.
claims.believers: Users describe it as cheaper and easier to reverse than filler [11].
claims.experts: A Google Trends analysis found lip flip searches growing but below lip filler searches from 2014 to 2024 [10].

card.summary: Botox in the upper lip muscle to roll the lip out; temporary, with only small studies behind it.
card.note: Off-label use; the term "lip flip" is also used for a filler technique.

quick.overview:
A lip flip uses small injections of botulinum toxin around the upper lip so it rolls slightly outward, showing a bit more pink lip without adding volume.

Evidence consists of case series, reviews and a 2025 systematic review. Forum users discuss it as a reversible way to change a thin upper lip.
quick.mechanism: Botulinum toxin weakens part of the orbicularis oris muscle, so the lip border everts and the lip looks fuller. Effects are described as lasting about three to four months.
quick.risks: Off-label use. Weakening muscles near the mouth can affect symmetry and function; published abstracts give no firm complication rates. Medical sources describe it as clinician-performed.
